events.title: Community Open House Jam at RBC
events.address: 214 N Pokegama Ave, Grand Rapids, MN
events.description: Join us for an afternoon of live music, community, and celebration as we honor four families whose musical traditions have left a lasting mark on Grand Rapids: the LaPlant, Miltich, Downing, and Aultman families. Community Open House Jam Sunday, September 20, 2026 2:00 PM – 7:00 PM Rapids Brewing Co., Grand Rapids, MN Whether you’re a lifelong musician, an occasional picker, or simply someone who loves great music and local history, you’re invited to be part of this special gathering. Bring your instrument and join the open jam sessions or sit back and enjoy an afternoon filled with music, storytelling, and community spirit. Hosted by Kari Hedlund of KAXE, the event will also feature displays of historical family photographs and two ceremonial toasts at 3:00 PM and 5:30 PM celebrating the enduring contributions of these remarkable families to the cultural life of Grand Rapids. Food and beverages will be available for purchase from Rapids Brewing Company throughout the event. This is a celebration of legacy, friendship, and the power of music to bring people together across generations. Everyone is welcome! Admission is free. Special thanks to Rapids Brewing Company, KAXE, the Reif Arts Council, and the Grand Rapids community for helping make this celebration possible. Free to attend Free to listen Free to play

It is a clap along, sing along musical comedy show where the audience is always a part of the action! No one does it better than Dave and Ted. For a pair of self-taught pianists from Minnesota, David Eichholz and Ted Manderfeld have mastered the sophisticated nuances of burlesque’s best ribald and bawdy traditions. Deuces Wild! Dueling Pianos offers a Las Vegas-style show of comedy and extensive audience participation featuring an unlikely and surprising mix of music and parodies that range from classic rock and country to rap and show tunes. The key to their marathon of musical comedy, however, is the unabashed and completely liberated participation of audience members from 18 to 80. This event is not eligible for any discounts. events.title: Duluth Does The Dead
events.description: Calling all Deadheads! More than two dozen Twin Ports musicians will pay tribute to the Grateful Dead performing some of the band’s biggest songs at 7 pm Saturday, Sept. 26. This one-night-only concert is part of an ongoing tribute series staged at Sacred Heart Music Center twice a year. Each Northland artist will perform a song from the Grateful Dead’s huge and diverse catalog. Expect an endless jam! All proceeds from this Duluth Does concert goes to support Sacred Heart Music Center programming and maintenance of its historic property. Kim Curtis Monson of The Fish Heads will serve as MC. Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $18 at 10 a.m. Tuesday, Sept. 1 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $15 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $15 (plus $1 handling fee). events.title: Organ concert: From Baroque to Classical Brilliance
events.description: The Friends of the Felgemaker proudly present “From Baroque to Classical Brilliance.” This event will be a grand afternoon of classical masterpieces featuring the historic Felgemaker pipe organ and an intimate chamber orchestra. The concert showcases magnificent works by three legendary 18th Century composers: George Frideric Handel, Joseph Haydn, and Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart. Performing the music will be Sacred Heart Music Center’s Resident Organist, Dr. Charles Sundquist, who will be joined by some of the region’s finest orchestral players: Laurie Bastian and Kristin Sande, violin; Kevin Hoeschen, viola; Byron Klimek, cello; Brett Linski and Madeline Miller, oboe; and Tom Pfotenhauer and Stacy Carolan, on trumpet. Come hear this chamber music program combining the thrilling power of the Felgemaker pipe organ with the grace of a chamber orchestra in Sacred Heart Music Center’s renowned acoustical space. Advance e-tickets are $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE and will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. Student rush tickets are $5 at the door. The concert will be presented Sunday, Sept. 27. Doors at 2 pm. Music at 3.

events.title: Jaerv and OK Factor
events.description: Legendary Swedish group Jaerv and Twin Cities-based duo OK Factor return to the beautiful Sacred Heart alter stage Friday, Oct. 16. The award-winning Jaerv present an extroverted, vigorous and heartfelt folk music with influences from both jazz and pop music. The group offers a varied stage performance where five-voiced tunes blend in with energetic dances and free improvisations. Jaerv is an internationally well known act and has toured the U.S., Japan, Spain, Scotland, Ireland, Finland and Norway among other countries. Their discography includes three full length albums. New classical crossover group OK Factor was formed more than 10 years ago by cellist Olivia Diercks and violinist Karla Peters. Organic and genuine, their original compositions and arrangements feel both comfortingly familiar and uniquely fresh. The group has toured nationally, internationally and recorded five studio albums of original work. Advance E-tickets will be available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE beginning at 10 a.m Friday, Sept. 11. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 (Student rush $10) while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold album release concert
events.description: Duluth-based Americana group Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold celebrate the release of their new album “Dedication.” Steeped in musical traditions of folk, bluegrass, country, classic rock, and blues, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold offers a genre-blending sound that is captivating, invigorating, and sure to get your toe tapping. After two decades of writing songs and performing as a solo artist, Danny Frank released of his debut album “Smoky Gold” in 2021. He then assembled an all-star cast of seasoned musicians to fully compliment his music. “The Smoky Gold” is comprised of banjo player Harrison Olk (Tin Can Gin, Cascade Crescendo, Kind Country Band), bassist Joe Scarpellino (Smokin’ Joe, Dead Larry), and fiddle savant Erin Aldridge (Concert Master – Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra). Together the group has recorded and released the full length album “Dedication.” Opening the evening will be Adam Greuel (Horseshoes & Hand Grenades) and Kenny Leiser (Joseph Huber). Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $20 (plus $3.18 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $20 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $20 (plus $1 handling fee). Tickets will be available at the door for $25 while supply lasts. Doors at 6 :30 pm. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Silent Film: The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari
events.description: Organist Aaron David Miller accompanies the classic 1920 silent horror film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari.” The Friends of The Felgemaker invite you to experience what it was like to attend a silent movie! Renowned organist Aaron David Miller will accompany the silent film “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” at 7 p.m. Friday, Oct. 23 on the historic Felgemaker pipe organ housed at Sacred Heart Music Center. “The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari” is a groundbreaking German horror film which set standards for creative camera work and featured a dark and twisted style of storytelling. It is widely considered the first true horror story put to film. Aaron David Miller is noted for his highly imaginative and creative style, found in his performances, improvisations and compositions. He has won numerous international awards for improvisation and has given concerts and accompanied silent films across the country. Advance adult tickets are $20 (plus a $3.18 handling fee) and are available on Eventbrite HERE. Tickets will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. All students can pay $5 at the door. Doors at 6 pm. Show at 7.

events.title: Black Parade Duluth – A My Chemical Romance Tribute
events.description: Duluth artists celebrate the 20th anniversary of My Chemical Romance’s classic album “The Black Parade.” Considered an emo rock masterpiece, the concept album “The Black Parade” is a career defining work from American rock band My Chemical Romance. The full album will be performed by an all-star Duluth band featuring members from Jumpsuit, Between Howls, Gemstones, Danny Frank & The Smoky Gold, The Draco Volans, Duluth Transit Authority, and many more. Duluth-based Ephemera opens. Advance e-tickets will go on sale for $15 (plus $2.85 in fees) at 10 a.m. Friday, Sept. 11 on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available at Globe News in Superior for $15 (cash only) and Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth for $15 (plus $1 handling fee). Tickets will be available at the door for $20 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30 pm. Music at 7:30.

events.title: Mason Jennings
events.description: Minnesota troubadour Mason Jennings returns performing old favorites and work from his new album “Dark Wings.” “I love song craft,” says Mason Jennings, a folksinger who has spent over two decades honing his craft both on stage and in the studio. “A song is like a boat on the water, and you’re trying to make it float with as few pieces as possible. If you do it right, a song can be very healing.” For Jennings, songwriting has always been about a personal connection, both with his audience and himself. He’s known for an unpretentious, emotive approach to folk music, combining introspective lyrics with acoustic melodies. His work has drawn comparisons to genre greats, including Nick Drake, John Fahey, and Tom Waits. But Jennings’ sound is distinctly his own, one that blends vulnerability with strength, simplicity with complexity. That style comes through on his new record: “Dark Wings.” His 18th studio album, the record finds Jennings moving between raw honesty about childhood scars, dark thoughts, spiritual questioning and a stubborn belief in the power of love. Duluth-based singer-songwriter and bandleader Breanne Marie of Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners will open with a solo set. Advance E-tickets are available for $25 (plus $3.52 in fees) on Eventbrite HERE. Paper tickets will be available for $25 at Zenith Bookstore in West Duluth (plus $1 handling fee) and at Globe News in Superior (cash only). Tickets will be available at the door for $30 while supply lasts. Doors at 6:30. Music at 7:30.

events.title: An Evening with New York Times Author William Kent Krueger
events.description: Please join Zenith Bookstore for a very special evening at Clyde Iron Works (upstairs) on Friday, September 4th 7 PM. New York Times best-selling author William Kent Krueger will share his brand-new book, God’s Country. If you have heard Kent speak before, you know you are in for an entertaining and captivating night! So, invite a friend or two. Books will be available for purchase that night or you can pre-order them through Zenith and Kent will be available to personally autograph your book at the event. Also, Clyde Iron Works will offer full bar service in our space. In God’s Country, Cork O’Connor, prepares for a family trip into the Boundary Waters, but he is troubled by ominous visions about his future. Ignoring the warnings, he uncovers signs of violence while searching for his missing friend, Cordell Bishop. Soon, he is forced to negotiate with dangerous criminals, the Kennedy brothers, who are seeking their late father’s hidden stash. William Kent Krueger is the New York Times bestselling author of The River We Remember, This Tender Land, Ordinary Grace (winner of the Edgar Award for best novel), and the original audio novella The Levee, as well as twenty-one acclaimed books in the Cork O’Connor mystery series, including Apostle’s Cove, Spirit Crossing, and Fox Creek. He lives in the Twin Cities with his family. See our website or Facebook page for more details.

events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion
events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. Our narrated tour takes you along the original Lake Superior & Mississippi line in vintage coaches. Go where cars and hiking boots can’t reach. The St. Louis River Estuary is a hidden sanctuary for bald eagles, osprey, and Northland wildlife. Bring your camera for unparalleled views of the Duluth riverfront. Best to arrive about a half-hour before departure. Our ticket office is located just off of Grand Avenue.

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

Whether you’re visiting Duluth for the weekend or looking for something fun to do with the kids this summer, the Family Fun Cruise is an easy addition to your day. Enjoy fresh air, waterfront views, family-friendly activities, and plenty of opportunities for photos and memories together. Snacks, beverages, and a full bar are available for purchase onboard. One-hour cruise aboard the Vista Queen Activities designed for kids Affordable family fun Perfect timing for young families Beautiful harbor and Lake Superior views Bring the whole crew and make some memories on the water this summer! events.description: High Key Mondays & Industry Night Are BACK! Live local music | Drink specials | 6–9pm High Key Monday is FRI-YAY for many of our industry partners — and we’re roll with it. Calling all restaurant, bar, liquor store, and brewery professionals in the Twin Ports — get on down to the Paddle for Industry Night! Show a worker ID or pay stub for $1 off all Bent Paddle beverages. Thank you for keeping our paddles in the water! Everyone is welcome! Come for the tunes, stay for the conversations, delicious beverages, and good times. This month to kick off and celebrate the return, we invite you to connect with local organizations making waves in the Twin Ports — like WE Health, Trans+ Northland, Twin Ports Artists Collective, and Men As Peacemakers. events.description: Think you’ve got the brains and the bravado? Join us for Trivia Night at the Zoo, happening the second Wednesday of every month inside the Porcupine Pub at Lake Superior Zoo. events.title: Two T’s In A Pod + Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners | Live Music in The Yard!
events.description: Mother-daughter duo Two T’s in a Pod perform charming children’s songs, pop covers, and originals on guitar and harmonica. Together, Breanne and Anya Tepler create a sound that is unadorned, letting both of their personal vocals shine through. The pair’s single, “It’s Time to Go to Bentleyville,” is performed each year at Bayfront on the Bentleyville playlist. The duo has made an appearance at FinnFest, on Two Harbor’s Community Radio’s Beat Farm program, Wild State Cider Family Jam, Pikkujoulu, and other events. Great Lakes Country from a front porch in Duluth, MN. Bringing foot-stomping hometown country jams and soulfully sentimental ballads, Breanne Marie & The Front Porch Sinners delivers high-energy Americana. Featuring singer/songwriter and sometimes trumpeter Breanne Marie on lead vocals, the band blends traditional pedal steel with guitar lines, driving bass and drums which Americana Highways described as “a brilliant blend of 90s indie and country.” Whether winding through creative sonic landscapes or laying down toe-tapping bluegrass, their heartfelt lyrics and songwriting aim to warm even the coldest nights.

events.title: Lake Superior Live Cruise ft. Abe Curran
events.description: Relax on Lake Superior with live local music by Abe Curran, great food, and unforgettable waterfront views. Lake Superior Live is Vista Fleet’s summer music series, combining a casual harbor cruise, live performances from some of the Twin Ports’ favorite musicians, and a BBQ-style dinner. Whether you’re looking for a unique date night, a fun evening with friends, or simply an excuse to get out on the water, this cruise offers a laid-back way to enjoy Duluth’s waterfront. Weather permitting, cruises travel through both the Duluth Canal and Superior Entry, offering incredible views of Lake Superior, working waterfront activity, and the Duluth skyline. Your ticket includes a casual BBQ dinner. Grab a drink from the bar, find your favorite seat, and enjoy an evening of live music as the sun begins to set over the harbor. A full bar is available onboard with beer, wine, cocktails, soft drinks, and non-alcoholic options available for purchase.

events.description: Join us for a special Candlelight Concert featuring the Duluth Symphonic Winds performing live from Glensheen’s historic Terrace. Surrounded by the glow of candlelight and the beauty of the estate at dusk, guests will enjoy a musical journey spanning the early 1900s through the 50s, including pieces inspired by twilight and selections celebrating the history and spirit of the North Shore, shipping, railroads, and the ore docks. Check-in begins at 6:30 p.m. The first 60 guests will receive guaranteed seating in the Formal Garden, with additional seating available on the South Lawn. Throughout the evening, candlelit seating, illuminated mansion views, and the backdrop of Lake Superior will create a one-of-a-kind concert experience. Tickets: $10 per person Please note: Admission includes the outdoor concert only and does not include access to the mansion. In the event of inclement weather, the rain date is Tuesday, September 15, 2026. To purchase tickets, visit z.umn.edu/candlelightconcert Event Cost $10.00

events.title: Science on Deck
events.description: Welcome aboard the R/V Blue Heron! The LLO Science on Deck event is free and will take place from 11 am to 3 pm. Enjoy guided tours of the research vessel from the crew, interact with graduate students working on freshwater research, and explore engaging displays. The public can hear a presentation at 1:30 pm from the Large Lakes Observatory’s Dr. Ted Ozersky titled “What Lakes Do In Winter.” Location: (DECC) Twin Ports Harbor near the Great Lakes Aquarium at 353 Harbor Drive, Duluth, MN. ABOUT LLO: Located on the Duluth campus of the University of Minnesota Duluth, LLO is the only institute in the country dedicated to the study of large lakes throughout the world. They focus on the global implications of investigations in the areas of aquatic chemistry, circular dynamics, geochemistry, acoustic remote sensing, plankton dynamics, sedimentology and paleoclimatology. The Large Lakes Observatory serves as a basis for assessing human impact on large-lake ecosystems, and for developing sound policy for protecting these invaluable bodies of freshwater as our global environment evolves.

events.description: A Chorus Line is a groundbreaking musical that pulls back the curtain on the lives of performers fighting for a spot in a Broadway ensemble. events.title: Lake Superior Harvest Festival
events.description: Celebrating Food, Farmers and Community It’s the 32nd Anniversary of Harvest Festival!! Brought to you by the Sustainable Farming Association, “celebrating food, farmers, and community.” Farmers Market Live Music all day Nonprofit Expo Art & Craft Fair Energy Fair Food Court Educational Demos This is a free, family oriented event! We ask for a donation at the door to help support the festival and we suggest $5/person or $10/family, or pay what you can. It is $10 to park at Bayfront, and there is accessible parking closer to the entrance. We encourage you to walk/bike/bus/carpool!We suggest you bring your reusable bags and utilize our “park your produce” station at the LSSFA Info tent near the main entrance, so you don’t have to haul around your heavy veggies while you enjoy the festival. You might want to bring cash, though many (not all) vendors will accept a card, and we will have an ATM on site. Farmers market vendors will be accepting EBT, thanks to Community Action Duluth. Be sure to visit the Athena booth to explore innovative cultivation and crop protection products, learn about sustainable growing solutions, and connect with experts who can help improve plant health and productivity. And best to leave your dogs at home! This event started as a big farmers market, and has grown to be a huge community celebration. We do this in order to support our local farmers, other small businesses, and area nonprofits. We thank everyone who is involved in planning, and thank you for coming! For more information, visit sfa-mn.org/harvest-festival/

events.title: Duluth River Train Excursion
events.description: Ride the Lake Superior and Mississippi Railroad. A historic 2-hour rail journey through the majestic St. Louis River Estuary. Family-friendly, volunteer-run, and purely Duluth. Our narrated tour takes you along the original Lake Superior & Mississippi line in vintage coaches. Go where cars and hiking boots can’t reach. The St. Louis River Estuary is a hidden sanctuary for bald eagles, osprey, and Northland wildlife. Bring your camera for unparalleled views of the Duluth riverfront. Best to arrive about a half-hour before departure. Our ticket office is located just off of Grand Avenue.

events.description: Calling all fans of witches and crafts! Get ready for a special screening where you can work on your own craft project during the movie with the lights on in the auditorium. Starring Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman, PRACTICAL MAGIC 2 returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.description: Celebrate fall on Lake Superior aboard our Harvest Dinner Cruise on the Vista Fleet! Dinner includes your choice of Champagne Chicken, Roasted Pork Tenderloin, or Butternut Squash Ravioli, served with Butter & Chive Whipped Potatoes, Sautéed Green Beans Almondine, Black Woods House Salad, and a roll with butter. Dessert is also available to add to your reservation for a sweet ending to your evening. The Harvest Dinner Cruise is open to all ages and reservations are required. Join us for one of the best ways to experience fall in Duluth; from the water!

events.title: Bat Night at Minnesota Point
events.description: Join bat biologists as they investigate a group of nocturnal creatures that call Minnesota Point home, BATS! While a few surveys have been done there is still a lot we do not know about these insect-devouring locals, come out and see how we plan to change that. *This event is highly weather dependent; September 15th & 17th will be back up rain dates. For updates on the event please keep an eye on the Park Point Community Club and the Minnesota Scientific & Natural Areas’ Facebook pages or email arika.mcgraw@state.mn.us to be added to an email notification list.* The evening will start at the Walter F. Stock Pumping station so make sure to factor in the time needed to hike the 0.8 mile of trail from the parking area. This event starts at 7 pm and will include an introduction to the bats of Minnesota, what the Minnesota DNR and the US Fish and Wildlife service are working on with bats, Indigenous storytelling, and bat survey opportunities. Observe DNR mammologists as they gather bats that were caught in carefully placed nets to bring back to a processing tent near the pumping station. There they will record information such as species before releasing them. Others can join scientists as they go on walks up and down the beach using Echo Meters to record the sounds bats make to help navigate and find food. These devices are connected to a tablet and will detect and record the bats in real time. You will be able to see the color spectrographs of their echolocation and even get a potential species identification. Both of these activities will happen simultaneously and participants can filter back and forth between them. Park near the Sky Harbor Airport and hike 0.8 miles down the Park Point Nature Trail to the Walter F. Stock Pumping Station where the base of operations for this event will be located. *We will be on site after dark so make sure to bring a headlamp or flashlight to help light your way back to your vehicle.*

events.description: Build for What’s Next: Strategies for Modernizing Your Infrastructure, an executive discussion for IT leaders, will examine how organizations can modernize their technology infrastructure while making smarter decisions around networking, virtualization, compute and storage. The event will be hosted by technology services provider Tusker from 11 a.m. to 1 p.m. on Thursday, Sept. 17 at Black Woods Grill & Bar, 2525 London Road, Duluth, MN. The program will be followed by a complimentary executive lunch and peer discussion. Led by Tusker’s Nick Stover, Practice Director, Modern Datacenter; Ryan Hanna, Network Solutions Architect; and Jason Oliver, Enterprise Architect, and moderated by John Irey, Vice President of Unified Communications & Connectivity, the session will explore how organizations can build an infrastructure roadmap for the next 12–18 months, prepare for evolving business demands, navigate licensing and virtualization changes, and improve resilience, observability and operational efficiency. It will also provide practical insights into prioritizing investments across networking, compute and storage, determining which emerging technologies actually make sense for an organization, and benchmarking existing infrastructure using Tusker’s Data Center Modernization Scorecard. events.title: Duluth Oktoberfestival
events.description: We are bringing everything you know and love about the German Oktoberfest right here to Duluth, MN! So dust off your lederhosen, lace up your dirndl, and come join in on all of the fun the festival has to offer! The Duluth Oktoberfestival will take place September 18-10, 2026 and is located within the confines of Duluth’s iconic Bayfront Festival Park (350 Harbor Drive, Duluth, MN 55802). Duluth Oktoberfestival was recently ranked as the top authentic Oktoberfestival Celebration in Minnesota! Come out to Bayfront Festival Park and see why this iconic Oktoberfest Celebration ranks as the best in Minnesota!

events.title: Woodstock Bay Cleanup

Please check in with SLRA staff/volunteer for clean-up gear, and a waiver if you have not signed one electronically using the link below. If you are interested in volunteering, you can email Jordan at jordan@stlouisriver.org (or just show up). Groups and other organizations are highly encouraged to get involved. Save paper and time! events.description: Welcome to the home of the William A. Irvin Haunted Ship Tours in Duluth, Minnesota. That hint of cool breeze you feel isn’t just a change of weather. events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Book Signing: “Perseverance: A Memoir” by Mark Dayton
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: Join former governor Mark Dayton for a signing of his memoir Perseverance with a foreword by Hillary Rodham Clinton. In his own words, Perseverance: A Memoir details Dayton’s life story, including his childhood in a dysfunctional household, his political awakening, his early life in politics, and his friendship with Senator Paul Wellstone, whose call, “We all do better when we all do better,” served as a lodestar for Dayton’s ongoing work. The book ends with a postscript on our current moment in public life. In addition to providing an enduring record of recent political history, Dayton’s memoir offers case studies of problems being remedied swiftly under leadership motivated by empathy. Perseverance provides occasion for conversations of consequence and substance, today and for years to come. Mark Dayton served two terms as the fortieth governor of Minnesota, from 2011 to 2019. His other elected offices include state auditor and US senator. Get your copy of the book signed and meet Mark Dayton. Books will be available for purchase.

events.title: Rock From the Heart
events.description: A Benefit Concert for Aortic Health Awareness Rock from the Heart brings the music—and the mission—together for a night of high-energy rock and real impact. Arch Allies will deliver the legendary sounds of Styx, Journey, REO Speedwagon, and more, while Rock from the Heart’s own house band, Aortic Fire, brings a performance that hits close to home. Together, it’s a full night of arena-style rock with a purpose. This event is part of Rock from the Heart’s ongoing work to raise awareness and provide education around aortic and heart valve disease—conditions that often go undetected until it’s too late. Through music, shared stories, and community connection, we’re helping people better understand their risk, know their family history, and feel supported every step of the way. 5pm – Rockin Heart’s preshow party (for those who purchase the Rockin’ Hearts or Ultimate Experience tickets) 7pm – Doors Doors (for those who purchase General Admission and Reserved Table Seating) 8pm – Benefit Concert ABOUT ROCK FROM THE HEART Rock from the Heart’s mission is to proactively educate people about aortic and heart valve disease, bridge the gap between impacted families and the support they need, connect those diagnosed with vital resources, and inspire all through the healing power of music. Visit for more info: rockfromtheheart.org

events.title: Photography & Art at the Rock: Featuring Shawn Malone
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: September at the Rock celebrates the wonder of Lake Superior—by day, by night, and under the stars. We are proud to feature Shawn Malone, a landscape photographer and visual artist whose work has been inspired by the Lake Superior region for more than 25 years. After moving from Chicago to Marquette, Michigan, Shawn found both her home and her artistic calling along the shores of Lake Superior. Since then, she has dedicated her career to capturing the ever-changing beauty of this remarkable landscape—from rugged coastlines and dramatic weather to the brilliant colors of the aurora borealis and the quiet brilliance of the night sky. Best known for her immersive aurora and night sky photography, Shawn creates images and time-lapse films that reveal the beauty of the natural world in ways often hidden from the naked eye. Her work invites viewers to slow down, look up, and experience the wonder that unfolds after sunset. In addition to operating her Lake Superior Photo gallery in downtown Marquette, Shawn is an award-winning photographer, educator, and workshop leader. She has spent more than a decade sharing her passion for the night sky through presentations, photography workshops, and guided experiences throughout the Great Lakes region, helping others discover the magic of photographing Lake Superior under the stars. On display September 1–30. Meet the Artist: September 29 | 10 am–6 pm Experience Lake Superior through the lens of one of the region’s most accomplished night sky photographers.

events.title: World Ballet Company: Swan Lake
events.description: TICKETS Get Tickets Here Make it a group experience! Special pricing is available for groups of 10 or more: worldballetcompany.com/group-tickets. ABOUT THE SHOW The World’s MOST Iconic Ballet – With a LIVE Orchestra! The legendary tale of Swan Lake takes flight in a breathtaking production from World Ballet Company, as fate and magic entwine in a timeless battle between good and evil. Performing with a Live Orchestra, and featuring a cast of 50 international dancers, over 150 radiant hand-sewn costumes, and stunning hand-crafted sets, this spellbinding ballet captures every heart-pounding moment – from the Dance of the Little Swans to the Black Swan’s 32 fouettés, and every pirouette in between. With Tchaikovsky’s unforgettable score soaring through the air and played LIVE, immerse yourself in this mesmerizing journey where dreams, heartbreak, and hope unfold right before your eyes. Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes (including 20-minute intermission) Audience: For ages 5 & over ABOUT WORLD BALLET COMPANY World Ballet Company – Ballet Everywhere, Ballet For All. Based in Los Angeles, and led by Sasha Gorskaya and Gulya Hartwick, World Ballet Company presents the most beloved and iconic ballets of our time in cities nationwide. Driven by the belief that ballet is for everyone, performances appeal to newcomers and seasoned ballet goers alike. The company attracts many international artists and comprises renowned professional dancers representing over ten countries. To date, World Ballet Company has traveled to more than 300 cities, reaching an audience of more than 500,000 fans. WBC Website: https://worldballetcompany.com/duluth2 KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.description: Hadestown, previously scheduled for March 16, 2026, at the DECC Symphony Hall, has been POSTPONED due to travel conditions and restrictions surrounding the Midwest Winter Storm. The performance has been rescheduled for Monday, October 19, 2026. All current tickets will be valid for the October performance. ABOUT THE SHOW COME SEE HOW THE WORLD COULD BE. Welcome to HADESTOWN, where a song can change your fate. Winner of eight 2019 Tony Awards® including Best Musical and the 2020 Grammy® Award for Best Musical Theater Album, this acclaimed new show from celebrated singer-songwriter Anaïs Mitchell and original director Rachel Chavkin (Natasha, Pierre & The Great Comet of 1812) is a love story for today... and always. HADESTOWN intertwines two mythic tales — that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of King Hades and his wife Persephone — as it invites you on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Mitchell’s beguiling melodies and Chavkin’s poetic imagination pit industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love. Performed by a vibrant ensemble of actors, dancers and singers, HADESTOWN is a haunting and hopeful theatrical experience that grabs you and never lets go. For more information, visit hadestown.com 2025-26 BROADWAY AT THE DECC SEASON LINEUP The Book of Mormon – October 28-29, 2025 A Magical Cirque Christmas – December 16, 2025 Tina – The Tina Turner Musical – February 15, 2026 The Music Man – April 29, 2026 Hadestown – October 19, 2026 BROADWAY AT THE DECC 2025-26 SEASON INFORMATION KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: Neural Exercises for Autism, a conversation with the author
events.venue: At Sara’s Table Chester Creek Cafe
events.description: Is Autism an identity or a disorder, is an ongoing question which faces those who describe themselves under the umbrella of Neurodiversity language. WW Norton author, and autistic individual, Sean Inderbitzen LCSW, DSW, invites neurodiverse Duluthians to wrestle with this question with him in a small gathering setting. Themes to be covered from his new book in this talk include identity, temperment, disorder, empathy, and the role of ambiguous loss in shaping connection and rigidity. These themes like these and more appear in his new book Neural Exercises for Autism, and we invite you to meet with the author partaking in discussion, pastries, and a dive into meaning and neurodiversity. Please register for our gathering complete with readings, discussion, pastries from Sara’s Table at Chester Creek Cafe, and Alcoholic beverages available for purchase. Pastries will be provided for those who wish to partake, and beverages are guest responsibility. Our event is on a first come first serve basis. If you are unable to make it and register, please cancel as space is limited to the first 25 registrations.

events.title: 38 Special
events.description: Thursday, November 5, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT 38 SPECIAL Formed in 1974, the band toured tirelessly from the start, sharpening the explosive live show that’s been 38 Special’s calling card for a half-century. Along the way, the Florida natives fine-tuned their sound too: a blend of muscle and melody, filled with the arena-rock pop hooks that would soon become staples of FM radio. Years passed... trends changed... some band members retired from the rigors... but 38 Special remained, hitting the road year after year, flying the flag for an enduring form of classic rock & roll that never dies. As 38 Special enters its sixth decade together, the music continues with Milestone. It’s the band’s first studio album in more than 20 years, and it showcases a group of road warriors with plenty of miles left in the tank. Fueled up on snarling guitars, anthemic melodies, and the desire to break new ground, they update their sound for the 2020s, bridging the gap between past and present without forgetting their rock & roll roots. “After all this time, we wanted to create a more modern 38 Special album,” says frontman and co-founder Don Barnes. “This is a fresh, updated approach to the sound we’ve been making together for so long. Why not make a big statement after all these years? When you’re reintroducing yourself to the world, ‘good enough’ doesn’t work anymore. If you’re gonna do it, you might as well go big.” Learn more at 38special.com KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

ABOUT THE SHOW “An Astrophysicist Goes to the Movies – Part I” From Star Wars to Armageddon to Titanic to The Martian to oddly scientifically literate Beer Commercials. An entertaining and enlightening review of all the science that our favorite movies got wrong, combined with some of the stuff they got right. Incorporates recent films as well as some classics that you may not have known had any science in them at all. ABOUT NEIL DEGRASSE TYSON Neil deGrasse Tyson was born and raised in New York City where he was educated in the public schools clear through his graduation from the Bronx High School of Science. Tyson went on to earn his BA in Physics from Harvard and his PhD in Astrophysics from Columbia. In 2001, Tyson was appointed by President Bush to serve on a twelve-member commission that studied the Future of the U.S. Aerospace Industry. The final report was published in 2002 and contained recommendations (for Congress and for the major agencies of the government) that would promote a thriving future of transportation, space exploration, and national security. In 2004, Tyson was once again appointed by President Bush to serve on a nine-member commission on the Implementation of the United States Space Exploration Policy, dubbed the “Moon, Mars, and Beyond” commission. This group navigated a path by which the new space vision can become a successful part of the American agenda. And in 2006, the head of NASA appointed Tyson to serve on its prestigious Advisory Council, which guides NASA through its perennial need to fit ambitious visions into restricted budgets. In addition to dozens of professional publications, Dr. Tyson has written, and continues to write for the public. events.title: Edmund Fitzgerald: A Great Lakes Memorial
events.address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd., Two Harbors, MN
events.description: This annual event commemorates the sinking of the freighter Edmund Fitzgerald and the total loss of the 29 crew members aboard on November 10, 1975. It is also a time to reflect on the memory of all lives lost on the Great Lakes. The lighthouse, fog signal building, and visitor center will be open for visitors. Guides will welcome visitors and provide historic site and shipwreck information. Throughout the day, visitors can watch a film about Edmund Fitzgerald in the visitor center, or join a guided tour exploring the history of Fitzgerald’s final voyage. At 4:15 pm, the lighthouse will temporarily close while the names of the crew are read to the tolling of a ship’s bell, with a rendition of the Naval Hymn. Following the ceremony, the beacon will be lit, and the tower will be open again to tour until close at 6 pm. Be sure to bring a flashlight or headlamp as the grounds and trails are unlit. The weather is unpredictable, please dress accordingly. The event will be streamed on Split Rock’s Facebook Page and the Minnesota Historical Society’s YouTube channel. Tickets are offered online and onsite. Tickets only guarantee you admission to the site and program. It does not guarantee you a parking space or specific seating at the event.

events.description: Friday, November 13, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 7:00pm Presented by Pepper Entertainment GET TICKETS HERE ABOUT THE OAK RIDGE BOYS For more than 50 years, The Oak Ridge Boys have defined one of the most recognizable sounds in American music, blending four-part harmonies with an energetic stage presence that has earned them Grammy, CMA, ACM, and Dove Awards. With a legacy that stretches from their Gospel roots in the 1940s to their rise as Country‐Pop hitmakers, the group—Duane Allen, Joe Bonsall, William Lee Golden, and Richard Sterban—has delivered classics like Elvira, Bobbie Sue, American Made, and Thank God for Kids. Their music has produced multiple gold and platinum albums, over 30 Top Ten hits, and collaborations with icons ranging from Johnny Cash and Paul Simon to George Jones and Ray Charles. Today’s performing members are Duane Allen, William Lee Golden, Richard Sterban, and Ben James. The Oak Ridge Boys remain one of the most enduring and dynamic touring acts in the world, known for a high‐energy show that celebrates both their rich history and their continued evolution. Whether performing for presidents, recording fresh takes on their biggest hits, or exploring new musical directions with acclaimed producers, they bring the same passion that first propelled them to stardom. With decades of tradition, unmatched harmony, and a timeless catalog loved by generations, The Oak Ridge Boys continue to captivate audiences everywhere they go. events.title: Antique Appraisal
events.description: Bring your antique/collectible item for a free appraisal to the St. Louis County Depot at 506 West Michigan Street, Duluth, Minnesota. The St. Louis County Historical Society has arranged for Denny Mager of Northern Specialty, an expert in antique appraisal, to be at your service beginning at noon in the Union Lounge (outside of the Board Room), which is on street level. Follow event signage. Registration is in person only and cut-off at 2:30PM, so the appraiser can finish appraisals by 3PM. Guests are called up in the order that they are registered. You may bring up to two items per person for an informal oral identification and evaluation of each antique. If the piece is too large or fragile to be hand-carried, clear photographs with a description of any marks and labels will be sufficient. Past participants have thoroughly enjoyed the appraiser’s comments on what is always an interesting assortment of antiques and collectibles. This session is part of an on-going public education program offered by the St. Louis County Historical Society. Sponsorship does not imply endorsement of this or any other estate/appraisal service, and museum staff members are prohibited by professional ethics from making financial appraisals.

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 3 – Under Open Skies
events.description: Breathe deep, open your mind, and stretch your arms wide with us as we celebrate our vast American landscape. From the wide-spaced harmonies of An Outdoor Overture and Howard Hanson’s cinematic “Romantic” Symphony, through the celestial expanse of Jennifer Higdon’s meditation on loss, to Dvořák’s jubilant Te Deum, tonight we explore what lies beyond the horizon. Featuring the DSSO Chorus COPLAND An Outdoor Overture HANSON Symphony No. 2, “Romantic” HIGDON blue cathedral DVOŘÁK Te Deum Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Gobble Gallop
events.description: This Thanksgiving, join us for the Gobble Gallop — presented by Essentia Health. This 5K, 1-Mile, and Kids Run is Duluth’s favorite family tradition. Whether you’re racing or strolling, every step celebrates wellness, community, and the joy of moving together. Join us and be part of a Northland tradition that keeps hearts warm and feet moving! This event supports Safe Haven Shelter & Resource Center. A portion of the proceeds of the event as well as all partnership and participant donations go to helping Safe Haven continue their essential work in our community. The race starts between S. 12th Ave. E. and S. 13th Ave. E. on London Road, just outside the Rose Garden.

events.title: Duluth Winter Village
events.description: THE MAGIC RETURNS TO HARBOR DRIVE! Dates & Times: December 5–6, 2026 | Saturday & Sunday | 10:00 am – 4:00 pm Admission & Parking: FREE to attend! (DECC Parking is $10) AN EVENT UNLIKE ANY OTHER! For one weekend only, we’re bringing together the best of Duluth in one scenic location. The 10th annual Duluth Winter Village returns along the lake on Harbor Drive this December 5 and 6 from 10:00 am – 4:00 pm. The magic of local businesses, charming wooden shopping cabins, family-friendly activities, hot food, beverages (including beer & cocktails), and carolers continues to be a magical tradition. The festivities are held outside and inside at the Duluth Entertainment Convention Center. Visitors will appreciate: Our famous holiday-themed Experiential Bar “Tinsel Tavern” — featuring cocktails from Vikre Distillery Local makers & on-site Blacksmith Soup flights On-site holiday portraits by the Christmas tree Hollybeary Kid Store is back with more shopping options for littles to pick out for their grown-ups Animals, live caroling, 25-foot lit tree Small Children and Nursing Area by Duluth Mom Duluth Winter Village merch produced by our local vendors Hug-a-Hen by the Locally Laid Egg Company Lift Bridge, freighter views and bonfires The annual event began on the grounds of Glensheen Mansion in 2016 but moved to its new location in 2021. The Duluth Winter Village is unique from other area markets in that the vendors are all local businesses with retail locations around Northern Minnesota. Participants include Bailey Builds, Altered Abode, Y-ker Acres, Hucklebeary, Frost River, the Rainbow Room, NaturaLight, The Big Lake, Wintergreen Northern Wear, Lake Superior Art Glass, Ivy Moon and the Moon Market. Food and drink from the DECC’s culinary team, Positively Third Street Bakery, Hungry Hippie Tacos, Duluth’s Best Bread, Love Creamery, Scenic 61 by New Scenic Café, TBSP Waffles, Yes Cheese, and more. For more information, visit here.

events.title: DSSO Pops 1 – The Heart of the Holidays
events.description: Shows at 5:00pm and 7:00pm Kick off your holiday season with us as we partner with Peter Brennan’s Jeans ’n Classics to bring every era of holiday music to life. From Judy Garland and Bing Crosby to Joni Mitchell and Wham!, this show delivers nostalgic classics and modern pop-rock favorites accompanied by rich orchestrations and powerhouse vocals. Warm, joyful, and packed with singalong moments, it’s the perfect way to turn up the holiday spirit. Featuring Jeans ‘n Classics Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

events.title: Creepmas Parade Duluth
events.description: The Creepmas Parade is an annual outdoor costume parade focused on folklore, blending Krampusnacht traditions and Creepmas aesthetics. Participants are encouraged to respectfully dress up as winter myths, cryptids or any creature that resonates with them. Bells are the unifying piece of the parade and organizers encourage everyone to jingle and jangle along the parade route. The parade takes place on the first Saturday in December. The parade can be joined at any point along the route. More information can be found at https://www.creepmasparadeduluth.com/

events.title: Similar Dogs at Ritual Marketplace
events.description: Join Us for Similar Sundays from 1pm – 3:30pm at Ritual Marketplace with the Similar Dogs (@similardoggy). Joe Lindzius and Sarah Jane Hale perform their diverse acoustic repertoire. Food and drink specials. Great company. It doesn’t get more magical than this!

events.title: Hadestown: Teen Edition
events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Trivia Night at Lake Superior Zoo
events.description: Think you’ve got the brains and the bravado? Join us for Trivia Night at the Zoo, happening the second Wednesday of every month inside the Porcupine Pub at Lake Superior Zoo. Each night features a mix of animal-inspired questions alongside general trivia pulled from headlines, pop culture, sports, history and more – so whether you’re a wildlife whiz or a well-rounded know-it-all, there’s something for everyone. 5PM – Porcupine Pub Opens 5:50PM – Register your Team of up to 6 people 6PM – Trivia starts 7:30PM – Trivia wraps/Prizes/Last Call for Alcohol! Fuel your trivia prowess with local favorites from Bent Paddle, Earth Rider, Wild State Cider, and more. Grab a warm pretzel, a slice of pizza, or a variety of pub snacks, settle in, and get ready for the wildest trivia night in town. This is a 21+ event, and the Porcupine Pub is the only area of the zoo open during trivia night. With adult beverages flowing and questions that may wander into mature territory, this evening is best enjoyed by grown-ups looking for a smart, social night out.

events.title: A Charlie Brown Christmas – Live on Stage
events.description: Presented by Northern News Now Wednesday, December 23, 2026 | DECC Symphony Hall | 6:30 pm TICKETS Tickets on sale now! ABOUT THE SHOW Everyone’s favorite holiday classic comes to life in the touring production A Charlie Brown Christmas Live on Stage. Join Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Lucy, Linus, and the whole Peanuts gang as they produce their own Christmas play and ultimately learn the true meaning of the season. A Charlie Brown Christmas Live on Stage is a present the whole family can enjoy! Adapted from Charles M. Schulz’s timeless story of the spirit of Christmas, A Charlie Brown Christmas Live on Stage features the unforgettable music of Vince Guaraldi. There’s no better way to discover the magic of the season! Browse here to learn more. KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.title: DSSO Masterworks 4 – Across the Sea
events.description: Brace yourself for adventure as we explore the New World’s ties to the old. We set sail from Ancient Rome with Beethoven’s brooding Coriolan — a general destroyed by his own pride — before arriving in New Bedford, Massachusetts, heart of America’s whaling industry, with Stephen Paulus’ Sea Portraits. We close with Brahms, who poured the wreckage of his broken heart into one of the stormiest works in the repertoire. Featuring John Novacek, Piano BEETHOVEN Coriolan Overture PAULUS Sea Portraits BRAHMS Piano Concerto No. 1 Schedule, tickets, and more info at DSSO.com

events.title: Shucked
events.description: Sunday, January 24, 2027 | DECC Symphony Hall TICKETS Current subscribers can renew their subscriptions now until June 26 New subscriptions on sale August 3 Join the Waitlist ABOUT THE SHOW Maizy and Beau are getting hitched, when the corn that protects their small community starts to die. The town needs answers. But who will dare to venture beyond the borders of Cob County? Including the knockout songs ‘Woman of the World’, ‘Somebody Will’ and ‘Independently Owned’, this Broadway hit about an unlikely hero, an unscrupulous con artist, and a battle for the heart and soil of a small town, is not to be missed. Run time: 2 hours and 15 minutes including intermission. SHUCKED is recommended for ages 10+. SHUCKED contains adult themes, moments of adult language and a harvest of corny innuendo. For more information, visit shuckedmusical.com 2025-26 BROADWAY AT THE DECC SEASON LINEUP Clue Live on Stage – November 11, 2026 Shucked – January 24, 2027 Cirque Alice – An Acrobatic Adventure in Wonderland – February 4, 2027 A Beautiful Noise – The Neil Diamond Musical – April 22, 2027 BROADWAY AT THE DECC 2026-27 SEASON INFORMATION KNOW BEFORE YOU GO

events.description: Called “achingly beautiful, thought-provoking, powerful and prophetic” by Newsday, Anaïs Mitchell’s haunting, jazz-inflected folk opera delivers a deeply resonant and defiantly hopeful theatrical experience. Following two intertwining love stories – that of young dreamers Orpheus and Eurydice, and that of immortal King Hades and lady Persephone – Hadestown invites audiences on a hell-raising journey to the underworld and back. Inspired by traditions of classic American folk music and vintage New Orleans jazz, Mitchell’s beguiling sung-through musical pits industry against nature, doubt against faith, and fear against love.

events.title: Photo Submission Contest – 2027 Area Directory
events.description: We’re looking for stunning outdoor photos that capture the beauty, culture, and spirit of Itasca County! Submit your best vertical (portrait orientation) shots for a chance to be featured in our 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory and win Chamber Bucks to be used at any Chamber member business! Prizes 1st Place: $250 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured on the cover of the 2027 Grand Rapids Area Directory Photos used inside the Directory: $25 in Chamber Bucks + Photo featured inside the Directory Photo Submission Guidelines Orientation: Photos must be portrait (vertical) to fit the Directory cover layout. Location: All photos must be taken outdoors in Itasca County, MN. Content: Highlight scenic landscapes, seasonal beauty, outdoor recreation, our culture, or local landmarks. People may be included but avoid close-ups. Image Quality: High-resolution photos (300 DPI minimum) preferred; smartphone photos accepted if they meet quality standards. Branding: No visible brand names, logos, or watermarks. If a selected photo contains brand logos, they will be digitally removed. Original Work: You must be the original photographer and hold full rights to the image. Deadline for Submissions Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM CST How to Submit Click this link: Photo Submission Form Limit 5 photo entries per person. Judging Criteria Photos will be evaluated based upon: Uniquely highlighting the natural beauty and essence of our topography and landscape, culture, and/or local landmarks. Relevance to tourism and the outdoor Itasca County experience Originality Composition & visual impact Ability to achieve photo quality and clarity Disclaimers By entering this contest and submitting photo(s), you grant the Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce a royalty-free, non-exclusive license to use your submitted photo(s) in the Directory and related marketing materials (print, web, social media, etc.) used in promotion of our area. events.title: Chamber Board Member Interest
events.description: There’s a Seat at the Table. Could It Be Yours? LOOKING FOR LEADERS: Who care about business. Who care about our community. Who want to help shape what comes next. The Grand Rapids Area Chamber of Commerce is accepting applications for upcoming seats on its Board of Directors. Serving on the Chamber Board is an opportunity to bring your perspective to the table, help guide the priorities and direction of the organization, and be part of conversations that impact businesses throughout our area. Why Serve? As a Chamber Board member, you will have the opportunity to: • Help shape Chamber priorities, programs, and advocacy efforts. • Represent the perspectives and needs of our business community. • Build relationships with business and community leaders. • Contribute your experience, ideas, and perspective to the Chamber’s future. • Help strengthen the business environment in the Grand Rapids area. Who Are We Looking For? We are looking for engaged, thoughtful leaders who care about business and our community and are willing to actively participate in the work of the Chamber. Applicants must be affiliated with an active Chamber member business or organization, or hold an individual Chamber membership. We welcome applicants from different industries, backgrounds, business sizes, and areas of experience who can bring valuable perspectives to the table. What Do We Need From You? You do not need to have prior board experience or be an expert on every issue facing our business community. We are looking for Board members who are willing to: • Show up and participate in Board discussions and decisions. • Ask questions and bring your perspective to the table. • Respond to Board email inquiries, including time-sensitive votes and requests for input. • Represent the Chamber and its membership in a positive and professional way. • Participate in and volunteer at Chamber events, as you are able. What Is the Commitment? Board terms are available for three years. The Board meets eigh

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: City Council Meeting
events.description: In-Person Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meetings are open to the public and held in council chambers at the Proctor Area Community Center (PACC) 100 Pionk Drive Proctor, MN. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6. Remote Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meeting is available remotely via YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@trac7298/streams. Public comments may also be submitted in advance of the meeting to cityhall@proctormn.gov up to 3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting with the e-mail title “City Council Meeting.” All comments are public data

events.title: National First Responder Day
events.description: National First Responders Day on October 28 recognizes the heroic men and women who make it their business to take immediate action when disaster strikes. Not sure what a first responder does? Just think about 9/11 for a moment. Firefighters, police, paramedics, and more — rushing into Lower Manhattan. Whether you’ve had your own emergency or not, it’s not hard to understand and appreciate the dangerous and difficult work they do.

Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6. Remote Access The 6:00 p.m. City Council Meeting is available remotely via YouTube https://www.youtube.com/@trac7298/streams. Public comments may also be submitted in advance of the meeting to cityhall@proctormn.gov up to 3:00 p.m. the day of the meeting with the e-mail title “City Council Meeting.” All comments are public data

events.title: Retail Employee Day
events.description: Today the City of Proctor proudly recognizes the hardworking team at Mountain Spirits Municipal Liquor Store in honor of Retail Employees’ Day. Retail Employees’ Day celebrates the dedicated people who keep stores running and ensure customers have a positive shopping experience. From helping customers find the perfect bottle, stocking shelves, managing inventory, and keeping the store welcoming and organized, retail employees play an important role in connecting products with the people who enjoy them. At Mountain Spirits, our team works year-round to provide friendly service, maintain a well-stocked store, and support this City or Proctor’s municipal enterprises. Their efforts help make shopping easy, enjoyable, and welcoming for everyone who walks through the door. Please join us in thanking the Mountain Spirits staff for their hard work, professionalism, and commitment to serving the Proctor community. Your dedication does not go unnoticed!

events.title: City Council Pre-Agenda Meeting
events.description: The 5:00 p.m. pre-agenda meeting is a work session between the City Council and City staff to review the upcoming City Council meeting agenda, future meeting agendas, and is a time for the City Council and City staff to have discussions about the agenda items and asking and answering questions. The agenda for the pre-agenda meeting is the same document as the upcoming City Council meeting agenda but does not follow the same format as the City Council meeting. Although pre-agenda meetings are open to the public, it is not a time for public comment, as the public can listen to the conversation and ask questions or provide input at the upcoming City Council meeting. Visitors should park in the North parking lot and enter Door 6.

events.title: Roller Rodeo -Roller Skating Event!
events.description: Saddle Up & Lace Up for the Roller Rodeo! 🤠🛼 Get ready for a night where the Wild West meets the roller rink! Grab your cowboy hat, lace up your skates, and join us for a Roller Skating Rodeo filled with country music, skating, and plenty of good old-fashioned fun.Admission is $3.00 per person. Skate rentals are available on site. We’ll be turning up the country tunes while skaters roll around the rink in their best western wear. Whether you’re an experienced skater or just looking for a fun night out with family and friends, there’s a spot for you at this rodeo! What to expect:🤠 Cowboy hats & western wear🛼 Roller skating🎶 Country music🌵 Rodeo-themed fun⭐ A great night with family & friends So round up your crew, put on your boots—or better yet, your skates—and come join the fun! Yeehaw... we’ll see you at the rink!

events.title: Celebrity Dance Challenge
events.description: 2026 marks the 20th Anniversary of Minnesota Ballet’s Celebrity Dance Challenge, an annual fundraising event that pairs local celebrities with professional dancers from the company for a fun and competitive evening of dance. Participants perform in a range of styles—such as ballroom, jazz, and contemporary—and audience members vote for their favorites. The event includes a social hour, refreshments, and a high-energy show. Social hour with appetizers and cash bar starts at 5:30; performance at 7:00 pm in the Depot Theatre. Proceeds from the Celebrity Dance Challenge support the Minnesota Ballet’s educational programs and its professional dance company, helping sustain its mission of artistic excellence and community engagement.

events.title: The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
events.description: Karl von Rabenau’s original choreography transforms Washington Irving’s legendary ghost story into the ultimate Halloween weekend event — a tale of rivalry, romance, and one very unforgettable ride through Sleepy Hollow. Performance at 7:00 pm on October 30, 2026 and 3:00 pm on October 31-November 1, 2026, at UMD’s Marshall Performing Arts Center.

events.title: Holiday High Tea
events.venue: The Great Hall at the Depot
events.description: ✨ Event Highlights: • Classic English Tea Service: Assorted sandwiches, sweets, scones and tea • Cash Bar: Specialty holiday-themed cocktails • Live Entertainment: A narrated synopsis of The Nutcracker by Minnesota Ballet dancers • Craft Corner: Decorate your own gingerbread cookie • Photo Station: Pose with ballerinas and Nutcracker characters in a turn-of-the-century-inspired setting • Discounted Minnesota Ballet merchandise & tickets available onsite 🎄 Special Offer for Families Receive $5 off children’s tickets when you purchase two or more using promo code TEA4THREE at checkout! 💎VIP Upgrades Available Treat yourself or someone special to the VIP experience, featuring: Priority seating at a private table A complimentary cocktail or mocktail A nutcracker-themed souvenir/toy Whether you’re continuing a family tradition or creating a new one, the Holiday High Tea with the Minnesota Ballet is a heartwarming way to celebrate the season.

events.title: The Nutcracker: A Duluth Tale
events.description: The holiday tradition that leaves every audience spellbound — this season featuring Tchaikovsky’s beloved score performed live by the Duluth Superior Symphony Orchestra. Performance at 7:00 pm on December 11, and 3:00 pm on December 12-13, 2026, at DECC’s Symphony Hall. Tickets available through Ticketmaster, or save more than $20/ticket in fees by calling the Minnesota Ballet Box Office (218-733-7570) to reserve your seats.

events.title: Figure Drawing Open Studio – September 2026
events.description: Artists must individually register online for each session. Check-in at the door is required. events.title: Weekly Creative Studio
events.description: $5 Members ($10 Non-Members) Weekly creative studio is FREE for DAI members at Collector, Contributing, and Benefactor levels Attend Creative Studio on the first Wednesday of each month to enjoy additional artist resources, special guests, and professional development opportunities during work time. events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!

events.title: Paddle & Pints
events.description: UPDATE: This outing is now SOLD OUT. Thank you to everyone who signed up! For those still interested, there are a few spots left for the September 19 outing. — Paddle & Pints 📅 When: September 10, 2026 | 5:00–7:30pm 📍 Where: MDC and the Glen Mine Pit Lake 💲 Cost: $40 🙋‍♀️ Participants: 21+ only, limited to 10 people 🔗 Registration: Click here! Experience an unforgettable evening on the turquoise waters of Glen Mine Pit Lake. Join Gary Kaunonen, MDC’s Education, Program, and Recreation Manager and Staff Historical Archaeologist, for a guided paddle before relaxing with drinks, a build-your-own charcuterie board, and, weather permitting, a lakeside bonfire. Your registration includes: ✔ Kayak and life jacket rental ✔ Guided one-hour paddle and shuttle transportation ✔ Beer, wine, seltzers, and charcuterie snacks (two drink max) Please bring: • Valid photo ID • Optional: your own life jacket Important Information: • Outside alcohol is not permitted. • Participants must use MDC kayaks; personal watercraft cannot be accommodated. • Non-alcoholic options will be available when possible. • Please notify us in advance of any gluten-free dietary needs. • Please bring layers of clothing and note that the red dirt does stain. • Wear appropriate footwear that you don’t mind getting wet or red. Space is limited to 10 people. This event sold out quickly last year!

events.title: Second Annual Night of Discovery Gala
events.description: ✨ Night of Discovery 📅 Thursday, September 17 ⌚ 5:00-9:30pm An Evening of Discovery. An Investment in the Future. Join us for Minnesota Discovery Center’s Second Annual Night of Discovery Gala on Thursday, September 17, from 5:00-9:30pm! It will be an unforgettable evening of celebration, entertainment, and philanthropy. Set against the backdrop of MDC’s beautiful campus, this special event brings together community leaders, supporters, and friends for a night dedicated to preserving Iron Range stories and expanding educational opportunities for future generations. Enjoy delicious food, signature cocktails, exciting raffle packages, and exclusive after-hours access to MDC’s exhibits and grounds. Throughout the evening, you’ll experience the impact of our work and learn how your support helps connect children, families, and visitors to the history, culture, and natural resources that define our region. The evening will feature live music from Minnesota’s own Sam Miltich & The Clearwater Hot Club. Born and raised in Grand Rapids, Sam’s instinctive jazz has captivated audiences on hundreds of stages—from Iron Range bars to New York’s Lincoln Center. His timeless sound will provide the perfect soundtrack for an unforgettable evening. Every raffle ticket purchased and donation made during the evening will support MDC’s Discovery Fund, helping provide financial assistance for field trips, educational programming, summer camps, workshops, and transportation costs so every child has the opportunity to learn, explore, and discover. Night of Discovery is more than a gala—it’s a celebration of the Iron Range’s past, present, and future. Raise a glass, make a difference, and join us for an evening where discovery creates opportunity. Cocktail attire is encouraged. 🎶 Live Music: Sam Miltich & The Clearwater Hot Club | 7:00–9:30pm Event Timeline: 5:00pm — Doors open 5:00pm-7:00pm — Social hour, raffle, and Discovery Pairings 5:15pm — VIP excursion for Premier ticket holders to th

events.title: The Research Center Presents: Become a Naturalist! Presentation & Book Signing with Teresa Veraguth
events.description: The Research Center Presents: Become a Naturalist! Presentation & Book Signing with Teresa Veraguth 📅 Date: Thursday, September 24 ⏰ Time: 5:00pm-7:30pm 📍 Place: MDC’s Theater 💸 Cost: FREE On Thursday, September 24, come on over to MDC to learn how to identify local plants, animals, and fungi with Teresa Veraguth! During her presentation, Teresa will explain how to use her book, Small Hands Can Help! Minnesota, as a multi-age, multi-layered tool to transform your family’s time outside into an ecological adventure. It’s fully illustrated, and it contains quality information, beautiful poetry, QR codes to scholarly resources, and more. She’ll also share how everyday citizen scientists can contribute to important environmental conservation work by observing the world around them, recording their observations, and uploading their findings to iNaturalist. It’s amazing how much of an impact you can make from your own backyard! After the presentation, Teresa will sign copies of her book. The evening’s schedule: ️☕ 5:00pm: Mingling and (free!) snacks (first come, first served) 👩🏼‍🏫 6:00pm: Teresa begins her presentation 🖋️ 6:45pm: Presentation ends, book signing begins 👋🏾 7:30pm: Things wrap up About the author: Teresa Veraguth is an author, illustrator, photographer, graphic designer, substitute teacher, and the founder of the Small Hands Can Help! book series. She is a graduate of UW-River Falls with a bachelor’s degree in liberal arts. She is passionate about ecology and education, and she envisions a healthy planet with joy for children of all ages. Her favorite naturalist topics are birds and pollinators. Check out her iNaturalist account! About iNaturalist: iNaturalist is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization that administers an online social network of people sharing biodiversity information to help each other learn about nature. As a crowdsourced species identification system, iNaturalist helps people identify the plants and animals around them while generating researc

events.title: Wild Roots Learning Community
events.description: Wild Roots Learning Community 📅 Dates: Sep. 10, Sep. 24, Oct. 8, Oct. 22, Nov. 12, Dec. 10 (all Thursdays) ⏰ Time: 10:00am-12:00pm (each time) 👧 Age Range: 3-12 y/o (younger/older siblings welcome!) 💵 Cost: $5/kid 3-and-older ⭐ FREE for MDC Members, kids 2-and-under, and accompanying grown-ups Wild Roots is a play-based learning group where kids discover the world around them through child-led exploration. This year, we’re exploring forces—wind, gravity, water, weight, and balance. A little wild. A little wobbly. A whole lot of wonder. 🔎✨ Potential weekly activities include making kites, building giant marble runs, testing boats in MDC’s outdoor pond, creating snow forts, building walkable bridges, and more. But the plan is always flexible. We bring the materials, give starting guidance, and provide encouragement, but the kids’ natural curiosity, burgeoning initiative, and trial-and-error problem solving skills bring the activities to life. Sessions may take place indoors or outdoors, so please ensure you and your kids wear/bring appropriate clothing—even once snow falls! ☀️❄️ Grown-ups are required to supervise their kids, but they get in free! 🪁 Session 1 (September 10) — Kites: Designing, building, and racing kites to see whose creations will catch the wind. Spoiler: Not every kite flies on the first try—and that’s the best part. 💨 Session 2 (September 24) — Pinwheels & Windsocks: Creating a field full of homemade pinwheels and windsocks. Kids get to redesign and relaunch anything that didn’t fly quite right the first time. More session topics will be announced as the season goes on!
